title: Second-chance page replacement
purpose: Show the clock hand skipping referenced pages while clearing bits until it finds a zero-bit victim.
requiredChecks: Before queue has pagesA,B,C,D,E with bits0,0,1,1,0 and handatC.
Inspection clearsC/D bits to0 and advances toE; A/B bits are unchanged.
After snapshot bits are0,0,0,0,0 with handatE, which is chosen for its zero reference bit.
The queues are circular and the rule1→clear/advance,0→replace is explicit; no referenced page is immediately replaced.
alt: Second-chance scan: clear reference bits for C and D, advance the hand, and select zero-bit page E
prompt:
Create a NEW original English technical educational diagram. White background, crisp large navy sans-serif text, flat blue/teal shapes, minimal clean connectors, generous margins, no logos or watermark, no decorative or traced textbook artwork. TITLE "Second-chance page replacement". Two clear panels "Before scan" and "After scan". In EACH panel draw the SAME circular queue of five pages A,B,C,D,E in that order CLOCKWISE. Use distinct labels inside each page node showing its name and bit.
Before bits: A R=0, B R=0, C R=1, D R=1, E R=0. A clearly labeled arrow "Clock hand" points to C.
After bits: A R=0, B R=0, C R=0, D R=0, E R=0. "Clock hand" points to E. Highlight E as "Victim".
Between/below panels, explanatory lines exactly "C: clear 1 → 0, advance" and "D: clear 1 → 0, advance" and "E: bit 0, select victim".
Footer exactly "R = 1: clear and advance · R = 0: replace".
The circular links must follow A→B→C→D→E→A, with no extra node, missing node or reversed scanning direction. After snapshot is immediately BEFORE replacement, so retain E as the selected victim rather than drawing an incoming page. Keep labels separate from arrows.
